observations.text: Re-review delta at commit 191f376. ARGV: git diff --stat 0bc44df 191f376; exit 0; stdout: tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_read_across_resume.rs (+254), tests/acceptance/support/review_app/repos_and_accounts.rs (+42), tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs (+4), .nwave/examine.json, scripts/examine/review-app-oracle and the feature docs and run records. No production file changed in this delta. The supports add three steps (when_her_store_stops_saving_reads, when_her_store_saves_reads_again, when_she_picks_the_run_up) over the existing ReviewApp::restart_refusing and restart_without_test_fault seams, and one constant REFUSE_MARK_REPO_READ whose value refuse_mark_repo_read is the fault name the app itself parses at crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs:314, so the seam it names really bites. Tree clean at 191f376.

The supports compile into every review-app target, so the whole package was built and run, not only this suite. ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app; exit 0; stdout: 22 test targets, 320 passed, 0 failed, 0 of them failing or erroring; the across-resume target reports 9 passed, 0 failed in 4.85 s. The three new steps and the new constant therefore break no existing review-app suite and no existing target's build.

I observed the reported RED myself with a resume-only mutation, and the two new journeys are the ones that answer the EXAMINE gaps. Mutation: in crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/resume.rs, PlanRowStatus::Read => resume.already_read.push(position) became PlanRowStatus::Read => {}, so the verdict drops every row the scan already read; nothing else was touched. ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 101; stdout: 4 passed, 5 failed in 6.46 s. a_run_cut_short_keeps_what_it_saved_and_the_run_after_it_reads_only_the_rest and repos_her_scan_had_to_read_again_are_counted_once_each both fail at left 2, right 3 over the three chosen repos, beside the two older journeys (left 2 right 3 and left 1 right 3) and L1/F101 (left {} right {1, 2}). Both new journeys are therefore falsifiers of the promise they carry and not green for free. Restored with git checkout --; the proptest regression file was removed; git status --porcelain is empty; ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 0; 9 passed in 8.34 s, so the restoration is observed.

The two added journeys close the gaps EXAMINE named, at the public port and without weakening anything. a_run_cut_short_keeps_what_it_saved_and_the_run_after_it_reads_only_the_rest answers E2: the run she picks up ends interrupted because her store refuses to save a read, her queue is read after the pause, after that interruption and after the last run, and it asserts that neither later run reads again what the scan had already saved, that the runs read her three chosen repos between them, and that exactly one repos-read line says three. repos_her_scan_had_to_read_again_are_counted_once_each answers E6: four runs with the save fault turned on and off, an assertion that at least two different repos were read by more than one run, the repos of each run printed, and the same count of three, so a count of repos is told apart from a count of read attempts. Both end on an interrupted or completed status asserted as a GIVEN-broken guard, so a scenario that stopped for another reason cannot pass quietly.

The printing added in this delta is output only and changes no observation: show_queue_evidence after each run in the journeys, and show_one_paused_scan guarded by a per-property static AtomicBool so each property prints one generated case. The guard is test-local, is read and written only inside the printer, and feeds no assertion. Timing after the delta: the target takes 4.85 s inside the package run and 8.34 s standalone on a cold adapter cache, for 9 tests of which four now drive the real binary over HTTP, still the share ADR-091 accepts for this family and far below the 300 s suite ceiling; nothing sits near half of its own budget, so no nine-run median evidence was collected. typesafe: unavailable, carried from the probe recorded this session (TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent from this process environment); every judgment here is locally derived from the measured runs and the read bytes.

diagnostic: Accepted, with no finding open. The delta adds exactly what the two EXAMINE gaps asked for and nothing that weakens the oracle. E2 is now observed by a journey in which her store stops saving reads, the run she picks up ends interrupted, and the run after it reads only the repos still owed while her queue still says three repos read; E6 by a journey of four runs over two lost reads, asserting that at least two different repos were read by more than one run and that the queue still counts repos and not read attempts. Both drive the real binary over HTTP, both assert the run status they depend on as a guard, and I observed both go red at left 2, right 3 under a resume-only mutation that drops the rows the scan already read, then green again at 9 passed once production was restored, with the tree clean and the regression file removed. The three shared steps reuse the existing restart seams and the fault constant matches the name the app itself parses, and because supports compile into every review-app target I built and ran the whole package: 22 targets, 320 passed, 0 failed. The added printing is output only and feeds no assertion. No design, implementation or product finding; nothing in this delta blocks completion.
